notes: Authored 2026-09-04 against the built brain for minimatch@10.2.6 (50 public symbols, 24 edges, compact format, schemaVersion 2). Brain module naming: the package's dual entry points are indexed as root modules 'esm' (import) and 'commonjs' (require), so every public API exists twice; expected symbols follow the lru-cache precedent and list both root-entry variants, which both truly answer each question. escape/unescape are indexed as definitions in the escape/ and unescape/ submodules (esm/escape.escape, commonjs/escape.escape, which carry the JSDoc); the top-level re-exports esm.escape/commonjs.escape alias them but are not listed as expected. Only escape and unescape carry doc text; every other symbol is grounding by signature only. Cases target documented real work: the dot, matchBase, windowsPathsNoEscape and nocase options on MinimatchOptions, list filtering/matching (filter, match), RegExp compilation (makeRe), brace expansion (braceExpand), escaping magic characters (escape), preset options (defaults), the reusable Minimatch class, and Minimatch#hasMagic (README-documented method for detecting magic characters). Tuning judgment calls: the natural phrasing 'How do I make the pattern * match dotfiles...' retrieved match/makeRe instead of the options interface, while prefixing with 'Which minimatch option...' ranks MinimatchOptions first; 'How do I turn a glob pattern into a RegExp object so I can reuse it...' pulled ParseReturnFiltered/MMRegExp and missed makeRe, while the imperative 'Make a regular expression from a glob pattern' ranks makeRe first. The windowsPathsNoEscape case only places MinimatchOptions at rank 5 (escape/unescape dominate because that option is documented in their JSDoc) but is kept as a natural phrasing. Considered-but-dropped candidates that were genuine retrieval misses after rewording: nonull ('keep unmatched patterns in the result list' -> ParseClassResult), nonegate ('stop patterns starting with ! being treated as negations' -> AST), unescape, and Minimatch#hasMagic ('check whether a pattern contains magic characters' -> assertValidPattern/AST); these are left out rather than kept as recorded misses, so there are no kept-hard cases: 12/12 cases retrieve at least one expected symbol in top-5 after wording tuning. 2026-09-04 audit: replaced the name-echo case 'Where is the 'Minimatch' symbol defined?' with the Minimatch#hasMagic task that the original authoring had dropped as a retrieval miss: a real README-documented question is worth keeping even when the engine misses it. Verified with TYPELATCH_USAGE=off npx tsx src/cli.ts query minimatch '<question>' --json --limit 5.
